entries.title: Reorder two requirements
entries.statement: For all propositions U and V, if (U and V) then (V and U).
entries.meaning: If both requirements hold, their order does not change what follows.

entries.title: Keep a fact while reusing a conjunction
entries.statement: For all propositions U and V, if (U and V) then (U and (U and V)).
entries.meaning: Use one established fact twice while keeping the original pair.

entries.title: Connect two rules
entries.statement: For all propositions P, Q and R, if ((P implies Q) and (Q implies R)) then (P implies R).
entries.meaning: Assume the two rules. Does the first condition imply the final one?
entries.lean: ∀ (P : Prop) (Q : Prop) (R : Prop), (((P → Q) ∧ (Q → R)) → (P → R))

entries.title: Check an insufficient requirement
entries.statement: For all propositions P and Q, if (P or Q) then P.
entries.meaning: An alternative requirement may be too weak. A failed search alone cannot refute it.

entries.title: Count joined lists
entries.statement: For all lists of natural numbers xs and ys, the length of (xs appended to ys) equals (the length of xs + the length of ys).
entries.meaning: The length of two lists joined together is the sum of their lengths.
entries.lean: ∀ (xs : List Nat) (ys : List Nat), ((List.length (xs ++ ys)) = ((List.length xs) + (List.length ys)))

entries.title: Reverse a list twice
entries.statement: For all lists of natural numbers xs, the reversal of (the reversal of xs) equals xs.
entries.meaning: Investigate a concrete list identity under the mathematical list model.
